title: The Great Fire of Rome breaks out
summary: A fire broke out near the Circus Maximus and burned for days, destroying large parts of Rome. Nero blamed the Christians and had many of them executed.
reason: The crowded city of timber buildings was highly flammable, and rumours soon claimed that Nero had wanted the fire to clear land for his palace.
significance: It led to the first Roman persecution of Christians and to the rebuilding of Rome, including Nero's Golden House.
